sections.content: How many people stayed in Cottenham after gaining qualifications?

Cottenham is a small town in the East of England. Cottenham does not have its own university.

Cottenham has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Cottenham ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 290 state-school pupils from Cottenham who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 140 (48%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 90 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Cottenham to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Cottenham's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Cottenham in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Cottenham's GCSE cohort:

  • 50 graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 35% of graduates living in Cottenham had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 85 graduates from our cohort living in Cottenham, compared with the 140 graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 65% of graduates had sat their GCSEs in Cottenham, while 35% had moved there from elsewhere.
